title: visioning cathedrals, capricorn ii
content:
this series is created for my collaboration with LJ of Ceremony for their communal writing practice, Atmospheres, based of the 36 decans of the astrological year.

Capricorn II — January 2-12
Key themes from LJ — relics, centuries, building
Before this: Capricorn I, Diamond Rain

*

during this first week of the year, I often notice an energy activation of great ambition, exciting new visions, ambitious plans. but, year after year, I saw that the year never turns out the way I plan it to be, and the weight of unmanifested dreams always felt heavy — it distracted me from what I did create, even if totally unexpected.

and so, in the recent ~5 years, I’ve softened this new year planning instinct in myself. I’ve deliberately practiced restraint from imposing what I want to happen — and instead, I try to sense into what wants to happen through me. it is a very fine dance between yin/lunar/passive/surrendering and active/Chariot/Mars energy of exerting my willpower and drive. I’ve made the priestess-moon my ruler queen, and the get-it-done Capricorn energy, my knight in arms.

~

this decan is particularly special to me, because it is the decan under which my partner K was born. in our four years together, I’ve felt deeply grounded and nourished by this energy. I felt that it stabilized my sense of inner chaos, such that my business and creative life flourished, with the support of his scaffolding.

I feel the combustion of Mars and Venus here, very acutely. I feel the deep grounding, stability, and ambitious drive — and I feel the inherent romance and dreamy nature of all the fantasy/planning. in both my creative life and in my relationship, the line between fantasy and planning, between imagining and materializing — it feels thin. this is both challenging and magical.

we talk about all the lives we could live, all the cathedrals we could build together. this is a deep form of romance, even if, on the other side, there is an acute fear — “what if it doesn’t happen? what if it was all a fantasy?”

this is why faith in the vision is so important. without faith, there would be no way to actually build the cathedrals. I think of the cathedral as an architectural container to hold the grandiosity and magnitude of the imagination. then, through its windows, I let myself be enchanted by the beauty of its light, of the possibility of transcendence.
